title: Room-temperature antisolvent synthesis of cesium copper halide nanocrystals

material.family: Cs3Cu2Cl5 example within the reported Cs3Cu2X5 family; other family outcomes and their incomplete recipe details remain in the source evidence and paper review.

missing_fields: No physical sample/batch IDs or cross-technique sample crosswalks are reported; context IDs here are descriptive only.
Charge amounts for Br, I, mixed-halide and CsCu2I3 routes are not supplied in the main text. Mixed-halide sizes, EDX numeric tables and full structural refinements are SI-only and unreviewed.
Cl TEM ±0.80 nm is accompanied by “(30%)” without a defined statistic; no particle count is given. Other mean sizes have no main-text uncertainty.
TR-PL 0.12–98 µs endpoints are not composition-mapped; Figure 5 Cl lifetimes are separate illustrative comparisons.
Figure 6a–c storage sample composition is not identified; do not assign it to Figure 6d.
Numerical spectrum coordinates, unlabeled plot points, TGA mass fractions and photostability time-series values are not extracted from plotted curves.
Matching SI (SHA-256 c6afc558d42c61cc99d4e0f44321fef222ec93d3563d186e40a1d1487527a8f2) is present locally but unadmitted, unread, and unused; SI-dependent details remain unverified.
General antisolvent conditions are room temperature/ambient; no numerical setpoint, addition rate or stirring speed is stated.
The precursor salt molar ratio for the detailed chloride example is 2:1, while the product crystal formula is Cs3Cu2Cl5; these describe different recipe-input and product-composition ratios.
74% and 95.7% are XRD crystal-purity estimates for different routes, not gravimetric yields. Figure 3b solution images in toluene and post-purification IPA redispersion are separate contexts.

Main Results text says EDX confirmed ratios across several formulas, while the Experimental Section describes EDXS characterization specifically for Cs3Cu2Cl5; full numerical SI tables are unreviewed.
